review_status: pending — a human must read this file against the domain repository (README.md has the checklist) before gate two refuses diffs with it

files.main.py: the entry point. A candidate that edits it can change which config is parsed or which rank reports — measurement, not structure.
files.generative_recommenders/research/trainer: the training loop and the eval cadence (eval_interval, full_eval_every_n, partial_eval_num_iters). Everything the metric contract promises about the window is enforced here, so a candidate that edits it can move the goalposts while its own diff looks like a model change. A hypothesis that needs a new `train_fn` kwarg is out of bounds by design; the encoder factories are gin-configurable precisely so structure work does not need this file.
files.generative_recommenders/research/data/ev: the metric definitions — hr@k, ndcg@k, the MAX_K clamp and the rank computation. An adjuster that can edit the evaluation cannot be compared with one that cannot.
files.generative_recommenders/research/data/re: the splits and the sequence construction. Changing them changes the benchmark and every number with it.
files.generative_recommenders/research/data/da: dataset loading and the eval target construction.
files.generative_recommenders/research/trainer: batch construction and the eval loader's shuffle, which the partial-eval truncation depends on.
files.preprocess_public_data.py: the data preparation the published numbers were produced with.
files.requirements.txt: dependencies. A candidate that upgrades torch is not a structural hypothesis and cannot be attributed.
files.configs/ml-1m/sasrec-sampled-softmax-n12: the baseline family's config. The round's baseline is HSTU at the whitelisted config; editing the SASRec config would change what 'the baseline' means.
files.configs/ml-1m/hstu-sampled-softmax-n128-: the published large variant, kept as published. It is the calibration point for the minimum effective magnitude, so it must not drift.

keys.train_fn.dataset_name: a different dataset is a different benchmark; the tolerance in the metric contract is calibrated per dataset.
keys.train_fn.max_sequence_length: changing the history truncation changes the benchmark, not the model — the README's rows are per length (the log directory is `ml-1m-l200`), so a candidate that moves it cannot be compared to the published HSTU numbers.
keys.train_fn.main_module: switching to SASRec redefines the baseline family. The README publishes one row per family at matched configuration; choosing the family is a human decision about what is being studied, not a candidate.
keys.train_fn.num_epochs: a training budget, and the eval window is 'the last epoch' — moving it changes both the cost and the number.
keys.train_fn.local_batch_size: an optimiser setting that also changes cost; a batch-size change confounds every structural difference in the same round.
keys.train_fn.learning_rate: optimiser retuning is a second hypothesis. Attributing a gain to structure when the learning rate also moved is exactly the attribution failure the one-change rule exists to prevent.
keys.train_fn.num_warmup_steps: same reason: every published config runs without warmup (0), so a warmup schedule makes the candidate incomparable to the baseline it is measured against.
keys.train_fn.num_negatives: the number of sampled negatives changes the scale of the reported metric: the README notes the BERT4Rec/GRU4Rec comparison slightly favours those rows because they used full negatives while the other rows used 128/512 sampled negatives. Changing it moves the number without moving the model.
keys.train_fn.sampling_strategy: in-batch versus local negatives is a different training signal, and the published rows were produced with `local`.
keys.train_fn.interaction_module_type: the scoring geometry (DotProduct) that the eval's brute-force top-k ranks with. Changing it changes what the score means.
keys.train_fn.top_k_method: retrieval implementation, not quality; it changes eval speed and tie-breaking.
keys.train_fn.enable_tf32: numerical precision. It moves the number and nothing about the structure, and it changes the experiment's directory name in exps/.
keys.train_fn.eval_interval: measurement cadence — the batch-level eval lines exist because of it, and none of them is the contract's metric.
keys.train_fn.eval_batch_size: measurement batch size: with drop_last and the truncation rule it changes which users are evaluated.
keys.train_fn.full_eval_every_n: the exact switch that decides whether an epoch's eval is full or truncated. Editing it silently changes the window the contract promises.
keys.train_fn.partial_eval_num_iters: how many batches a truncated eval keeps. Same reason.
keys.train_fn.save_ckpt_every_n: checkpoint cadence, not structure; it only moves disk usage.
keys.train_fn.l2_norm_eps: a numerical epsilon. A hypothesis about normalisation should change `user_embedding_norm`, not the epsilon that keeps a division finite.
keys.create_data_loader.prefetch_factor: data-pipeline throughput; it changes wall clock, not the model.

note: The adjustable surface: the paths gate two checks a candidate's git diff against, the gin keys a diff may bind, and the source symbols it may edit. `verified` records, for every key and symbol, the file and the exact evidence string that proves it exists in the domain repository — a name nobody can point at is a whitelist entry that refuses the wrong diffs, and `packages/core/test/generative-recommenders-pack.test.js` re-checks each one against a checkout when there is one. `forbidden` is not read by the kernel: it is the reviewer's and gate two's map of the tempting out-of-bounds changes and why each is out, so 'it was not on the whitelist' is not the only reason a human has to give. Anything not named in `files`, `keys` or `symbols` is out of bounds; the lists are exhaustive on purpose, because a whitelist that is 90% right is a gate that lets the one diff through that matters.
